submitter: bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path (retraction lane, extending sweep coverage per handoff 2026-08-08b §3.3)
rationale:
The daily review-queue sweep (revalidate_review_queue) now covers five item_types. claims_unverified is not one of them, and nothing else closes it either: `SELECT status, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='claims_unverified' AND status IN ('complete','verified')` returns ZERO ROWS on live clients_db (2026-08-09), and no row of the type carries a `deploy_result` payload, which is the tell that a real fix pipeline owns a type. Its producers set HandlerAgent "" by design, so there is no dispatch path, no handler, and no revalidator — 23 items across 7 sites, every one still `needs_human_review`. They are parked for ever by construction.

This is the same adoption this lane made for voice_tells on 2026-08-08 (council APPROVED r1, correlation 4d430ca8-7e34-479a-95f3-71fdc12fdef6), and it is being made the same way: run the CLOSER census FIRST (this lane once shipped a duplicate closer whose central claim was false and which 14 council seats accepted), share the emit-side scanner rather than restating its predicate, and make the scan report how much it actually read so that 'read nothing' cannot be mistaken for 'the copy is clean'.

ROUND 1 CORRECTION, and it was my error, caught by the editquality seat's gating objection. Round 1 claimed TWO converging producers (check_unverified_claims.go and check_unverified_claims_stats.go) and invoked the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §1 as the authority for shipping without an RFC. THERE IS ONE PRODUCER, so that ruling never applied. check_unverified_claims_stats.go registers no check, has no init(), and emits no WorkItemSpec — it is a helper whose scanStoredStatClaims() is called from inside ScanDeployedClaims (check_unverified_claims.go:385 pages, :427 chrome) and nowhere else in production. Its header line 'reuses the existing claims_unverified item type' means it contributes findings to that type, not that it files items. The seat's sharper question — is the SCAN LOGIC shared, not merely the item_key shape? — is answered by that same call graph: there is ONE scan and both halves live inside it, so the revalidator cannot judge by a second producer's predicate because there is no second predicate. The change is SIMPLER than round 1 described it and no longer leans on a ruling that does not cover it. Separately, (2) The scan has NO page-status filter, unlike ScanVoiceTells which restricts to p.status IN ('active','deployed'). That difference is preserved deliberately: the revalidator must judge by exactly the predicate the emit side uses, or the two ends of an item's life answer the same question differently — which is the defect this sharing exists to prevent.

Evidence that this judges real change rather than running inert: 16 of the 23 pages have a page_components.updated_at later than the work item's created_at. A 0 there would have killed the change; it was the disconfirming check and it was run before the code was written.

plan.summary: Register a claims_unverified revalidator in the review-queue sweep. Extract the emit-side claims scan into a shared, exported ScanDeployedClaims so the revalidator re-runs the identical predicate instead of a second copy of it, and have that scan report how many components it actually examined so 'read nothing' cannot be mistaken for 'the copy is clean'. Move the locked-component skip out of SQL into Go so pinned components can be COUNTED rather than silently dropped. The verdict ladder is a pure function with every arm unit-tested, and `resolved` is reachable only from 'components were read and were clean'.

edits.rationale: Extract the page/site query plus the claim scans out of UnverifiedClaimsCheck.Run into an exported ScanDeployedClaims shared by both ends, and export the evidence-base loader. ClaimsPageScan carries ComponentsExamined and ComponentsSkippedLocked because len(Findings)==0 otherwise collapses three different states into one: copy fixed, nothing read, and only-locked-components-read. THE LOCKED SKIP MOVES FROM SQL TO GO: the page query carried `AND pc.locked_at IS NULL`, which dropped pinned rows before anything could count them, so a page whose only claims sit in a locked component was indistinguishable from a page that was cleaned up. Emitted output is unchanged: Run filters to pages with findings, so the work items this check files are byte-identical. ClaimFinding is a type ALIAS for the existing unexported unverifiedClaimFinding — the revalidator must be able to name the type it iterates, and the unexported spelling has ~20 use sites including this package's tests, so aliasing avoids churn that buys nothing.

Run now calls the shared scan with an empty pageIDFilter and filters to pages that actually carry findings, so the check's emitted work items are exactly what they were before the scan was shared. This is the half that keeps the refactor behaviour-preserving on the emit side.

The drain itself. DB glue is split from a pure verdict ladder so every arm is testable without a database. Ladder order is load-bearing: 'still carries claims' is answered BEFORE 'some components were locked', or a page that still asserts a banned claim would be reported as unreadable rather than as still holding. Safe direction throughout: a wrong still_holds costs a human glance, a wrong resolved closes a live finding about an unsupported factual claim, so every arm that cannot answer returns `unknown`, which is non-terminal. The missing-page_id arm is also where the grouped site-chrome item lands — its item_key is the literal `claims:site_components` and its spec carries `surface`, not `page_id`. The item_key prefix is deliberately never parsed for a page id.

One map entry is the whole wiring: coveredItemTypes() is derived from reviewRevalidators, so registering the revalidator widens what the sweep selects in the same edit, with nothing else to remember and no second list to drift.

Every ladder arm exercised without a database. Two assertions are properties rather than cases: nothing reaches `resolved` without having examined a component (so a future reorder that closes an item on the strength of reading nothing fails even if each individual case still passes), and a fully-read clean page MUST resolve (a revalidator that can only say still_holds is the armed-but-inert shape this lane keeps finding, and registering one only adds scan cost).

This test pins the covered set and fails on any change, telling the author to update it and say why. It fired, as designed. The `want` list gains claims_unverified with the closer census and the two-producer note recorded beside it.

ROUND 3 — this is the OWNER'S ANSWER to the compliance seat's HIGH gating objection, which was raised identically in rounds 1 and 2 and which round 2 stated must be resolved by confirmed owner sign-off BEFORE the revalidator is wired live. The owner signed off WITH A CONDITION, choosing this over three costed alternatives (ship as-is; downgrade instead of closing; abandon). `resolved` now requires positive evidence that the PAGE moved: an EXAMINED component whose page_components.updated_at is later than the item's created_at. A register edit alone can no longer retract a finding. This is deliberately a mechanical control rather than a documented caveat, per the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §2 — a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share. The zero-filedAt case is a SEPARATE arm because x.After(time.Time{}) is true for any real timestamp: folding it into the comparison would make an item with no known filing date close on any component edit however old, the exact inverse of the gate. That defect was real and briefly present — the header comment already claimed the correct behaviour while the code did not, and the property test caught the difference.

Supplies the gate's evidence from the scan that is already reading these rows, so no second query and no second predicate. Tracked for EXAMINED components only: a locked component's timestamp records a change to content this scan deliberately did not read, which is not evidence about the copy the finding was raised against. parkedReviewItem gains CreatedAt for the other side of the comparison — one more column from a row loadParkedReviewItems already selects, and its SELECT and rows.Scan are now flagged in-comment as one contract.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-09, answering the compliance seat's HIGH objection from rounds 1 and 2 directly: sign-off GIVEN, conditional on the copy-changed gate now implemented. The owner was presented with four costed options (ship as-is; gate on the copy having changed; downgrade instead of closing; abandon) and chose the gate, on the reasoning that it converts a policy argument into a mechanical guarantee. Recorded in docs024/bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path/README_where_we_are.md and OBJECTIONS_2026-08-09_claims_unverified_council.md.

The gate is pinned by TestUnverifiedClaimsNeverResolvesWhenOnlyTheRegisterMoved, whose four cases are the ways it can be wrong: component edited before filing, edited at exactly the filing instant, no timestamp on any examined component, and no filing date on the item. Its fourth case FAILED on first run and exposed a real defect — the code disagreed with its own doc comment about the zero-date case — which was fixed in the code rather than the test.
plan.risks: 0) ROUND 3. The compliance seat's HIGH gating objection from rounds 1 and 2 is now ANSWERED BY OWNER RULING plus a mechanical control, not argued away: resolved requires the page's copy to have changed since the finding was filed, so a register edit alone cannot retract a claims-integrity finding. Round 2's demand — confirmed owner sign-off BEFORE wiring live, not concurrent notification — is met. The editquality gating objection from round 1 (the producer count) was a real error of mine and is corrected throughout; it NARROWS the change and drops a misapplied ruling. 0b) THE GATE IS NOT APPLIED TO voice_tells, which has the identical moving-standard hole. That is deliberate: voice_tells is live and council-approved, and its surface is style rather than truth — the distinction the seats themselves drew when escalating this type. Extending the gate there is a separate argued change, and is recorded as such rather than done quietly. 0c) The gate narrows what can close, so some genuinely-fixed pages will now refuse instead of closing — specifically any page fixed by an edit that did not touch page_components.updated_at. That is the intended direction (a wrong unknown costs a human glance; a wrong resolved closes a live factual-claim finding) but it does mean the type will drain more slowly than the 23-row population suggests. 0) ROUND 1 VERDICT WAS REVISE, gated by editquality on the producer-count claim; that error is corrected in the rationale above and in the register entry, and it NARROWS the change. One HIGH objection is deliberately NOT actioned and is escalated to the owner instead: compliance argues this is a policy-level narrowing of the human-in-the-loop guarantee on the platform's highest-stakes content-integrity type, and wants explicit sign-off from the owners of bugs_open/033 and /083 rather than notification. bug_historian and architecture independently routed the same question to a human. Seats agreeing it needs a human is the signal; it is not answerable by resubmitting with better measurements, so it is carried as a stated open escalation. 1) BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, STATED PLAINLY: claims_unverified items can now be closed without a human. The type was designed HITL-terminal and two open bug files (033, 083) tabulate it as parked work; their counts will move. Retraction is not the auto-rewrite the content-governance rule forbids — it never edits copy and never dispatches a rewrite — but it is still a machine closing a human-review row about a FACTUAL claim, which is a higher-stakes surface than voice_tells' style findings. Both files' owners are being told, not merely measured. 2) THE REGISTER IS A MOVING STANDARD, and here that bites harder than the voice gate did: evidence_base is DATA, so adding a fact row makes a previously unregistered number verifiable and the item retracts although the copy was never touched. That is arguably correct — the claim is now substantiated — but a `resolved` stamp on this type is NOT proof the copy was rewritten, and the two are only distinguishable by comparing page_components.updated_at against the item's created_at. Recorded in the concept register entry and in LANDMINES.md. 3) The no-register arm refuses the WHOLE item rather than judging per-finding. The banned-claim scan is fleet-wide and could in principle still be judged without a register; the unregistered-number and stored-stat halves cannot. Refusing wholesale is the deliberate conservative choice — the precision is not worth an arm that can close a live finding when it is wrong — but it means one item on a site with no evidence_base row will never resolve. 4) The locked-component arms are UNEXERCISED on today's data (has_locked_components is 0 across all 23 rows), so they are reasoned and unit-tested, not observed. They are written because the population will change and because a scan that examined nothing returns the same empty findings list as a page that was genuinely cleaned up. 5) THE SQL-TO-GO MOVE OF THE LOCKED SKIP widens what reaches the scan loop: rows that the query previously discarded now arrive and are skipped in Go. The emitted output is unchanged by construction (a locked row `continue`s before any scan runs), but this is the class of change where widening what reaches a function breaks it unedited, so it is called out rather than buried. 6) The scan has no page-status filter and this change does not add one, so an archived page is still judged. That preserves the emit side's predicate exactly, which is the point, but it means an item can resolve on a page nobody serves.
